samples.summary: Remote-change handler clears the image selection but not the in-flight resize drag, which holds the same stale-able coordinate
samples.evidence: The delta names "a remote peer's edit" as the second out-of-editor mutation source and handles it with `editor.clearImageSelection()` (docs-view.tsx:392), which is `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:3845) and only nulls `selectedImage`. But the repo's own documented rule for this class of state says the drag must go with it: docs-image-editing.md:341-346 and the `abortImageResizeDrag` doc comment (editor.ts:2581-2586) state that `imageResizeDrag` holds the same `(blockId, offset)` captured at mousedown and that "every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too, or the next `mouseup` commits the drag's size onto whatever inline now sits at that coordinate." `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2527-2575) commits through its own captured `blockId`/`offset`, independent of `selectedImage`, so a peer inserting text before the image mid-drag makes the mouseup resize the wrong inline. The only exported seam (`clearImageSelection`) cannot abort the drag, so the chosen layer — doing the clear in `docs-view.tsx` rather than inside the editor package — cannot satisfy the rule the design doc states; the updated doc bullet (docs-image-editing.md:358-368) also omits the drag entirely.

verdict.reason: The remote-change path clears only the image selection and never drops the in-flight resize drag. `store.onRemoteChange` (docs-view.tsx:392) calls `editor.clearImageSelection`, bound to `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:3845 -> 1295-1299), whose entire body is `selectedImage = null; render();`. `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2527-2576) commits through its own captured `blockId`/`offset` (2530), and `findImageAtOffset` (model/types.ts:457-467) returns whatever image inline now covers that offset, so a peer edit that shifts offsets mid-drag can commit the drag's size onto a different image. The repo's own documented rule requires the opposite: the `abortImageResizeDrag` comment (editor.ts:2578-2598) and docs-image-editing.md:341-351 say every path that clears the selection because offsets moved must drop the drag too. I searched for a counterexample beyond the reviewer's greps: the only `abortImageResizeDrag` callers are undoFn (2115), redoFn (2151), the commit path (2535) and resetAfterDocumentReplace (3958); `dispose` nulls it directly (3976); repo-wide `abort` grep in packages/docs/src shows nothing else; `EditorAPI` exposes no drag-abort seam; and `YorkieDocStore` fires `onRemoteChange` unconditionally (yorkie-doc-store.ts:564-579) with no deferral while a drag is armed. The design-doc bullet added for the remote source (docs-image-editing.md:360-369) also omits the drag, so the documented shape and the code diverge in the same place. Nothing refutes the absence claim.
